reason: The picture places mitochondria inside the cell, and adding them is part of the first goal.
expectation: The mitochondria will be added inside the cell.

alternatives.reason: The picture also places ribosomes inside the cell, so I could work on the other goal first.

effect: The mitochondria are now inside the cell; the glucose route and protein builders still need attention.
reaction: The placement matches the picture, which is satisfying.
reason: The carrier spans the membrane and has a pocket for glucose, so it looks like the route into the cell.
expectation: The carrier will be fitted into the cell membrane.

alternatives.reason: I could add the protein builders first.

effect: The carrier is in the membrane, and the new goal is to feed glucose to the cell to make ATP.
reaction: The two-panel picture makes the route into the cell clearer.
reason: The glucose matches the installed carrier's pocket, so I'll try feeding it to the cell as the new goal asks.
expectation: Glucose will enter the cell and help it make ATP, though I don't know the detailed process.

alternatives.reason: I could add the protein builders first instead.

effect: Glucose was used to make ATP; the picture links that process to the cell fluid, mitochondria and oxygen. The protein-builder goal remains.
reaction: The inset helped me see where glucose is used, though I don't know the detailed steps.
reason: The ribosome picture places these protein builders in the cell, matching the remaining goal.
expectation: The ribosomes will be added to the cell.

effect: Ribosomes are now in the cell, and the new goal is to give one an RNA instruction.
reaction: The enlarged groove makes the next pairing clear.
reason: The RNA copy comes from the nucleus, and the ribosome has a groove for an RNA strand.
expectation: The RNA instruction will be given to a ribosome in the cell.

effect: The ribosome now holds the RNA instruction, and the new goal is to build a protein using the amino acids already in the cell fluid.
reaction: The picture makes the connection between the RNA and protein building blocks clearer.
reason: The amino acids are a supplied pool rather than an item to select, so I'll check what the ribosome can combine with.
expectation: The compatibility list should show how to start building the protein.

alternatives.reason: ATP supplies usable energy, but I don't know whether the game requires it for this step.

effect: The inspection showed ATP was the missing partner and automatically completed the protein. The picture distinguishes ATP used for the work from amino acids that become the protein.
reaction: That connection between the two projects was satisfying; I hadn't been sure ATP was required.

mostWorthwhile.text: Building the protein was most worthwhile because it brought together the RNA instruction, amino acids and ATP, and showed their different roles.

leastWorthwhile.text: Adding the mitochondria and ribosomes was fairly predictable from their pictures, though it helped set up the later steps.

surprise.text: I wasn't sure ATP would be needed to build the protein; the final picture showed it being used without becoming part of the chain.

arbitrary.text: The ATP pairing wasn't obvious to me beforehand, but the compatibility hint and result gave it a purpose. I didn't find another action particularly arbitrary.

continue.text: I'd probably continue for another chapter to see how these cell parts connect to larger structures. The final connection was interesting, though some placements were predictable.
